proof.text: Put K=F[0]. Choose a K-injective resolution F[0] -> I and then a K-injective resolution t:A_U I -> J, using the resolution-existence theorem for module sheaves on the two sites. Exactness of A_U makes A_U F[0] -> A_U I a quasi-isomorphism, so J also represents A_U F. The adjoint of t under A_U dashv nu_U,* is a chain map h:I -> nu_U,* J. The definition of the derived comparison unit, followed by the final-object comparison, therefore represents c^q_{U,F} by H^q of Gamma(U_et,I) -> Gamma(U_proet,J). On chains this sends a section z to t applied to its comparison pullback: evaluating nu_U,* J at U gives J(U). Thus no assertion that A_U preserves injectives is needed.

proof.text: Write C=u_et,* I and D=u_proet,* J. The direct-image definitions give a canonical identity nu_V,* D = u_et,* nu_U,* J: at an etale W/V, both sides are J(W times_V U), and both restriction maps are those of J. Compose u_et,* h with this identity to obtain k:C -> nu_V,* D, and let d:A_V C -> D be its comparison-adjunction transpose. This constructs the chain map rather than assuming that an abstract direct-image isomorphism supplies one. By the unit-counit formula for transposition, the comparison pullback of a global section z of C, followed by d, is k(z). At the terminal object V, k(z)=h(z), viewed as a section of J on U, because both direct images evaluate there on U.

proof.text: The K-injective direct-image models identify $QC=Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}F$ and $QD=Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_UF$. Work first on complexes, writing $l=u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$, $r=u_{\mathrm{et},*}$, $p=u_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$, $s=u_{\mathrm{proet},*}$, $N=\nu_{U,*}$, $M=\nu_{V,*}$. Step 2 gives $\delta:Ms\cong rN$. The composite-adjunction definition and the unit-normalized conjugation lemma give its unique inverse-image conjugate $a:A_Ul\cong pA_V$, the canonical pullback comparison of the cited comparison node. Explicitly, precomposition with $a_X$ is the Hom-bijection chain $\operatorname{Hom}(pA_VX,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X,MsJ)\xrightarrow{\delta}\operatorname{Hom}(X,rNJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A_UlX,J)$. Apply this to $X=C=rI$ and $v=\varepsilon^p_J\circ p(d)$. Its first two adjoints are $d$ and $k$ by Step 2. After $\delta$, these give $r(h)$. Transposing under $l\dashv r$ gives $h\circ\varepsilon^e_I$. Transposing under $A_U\dashv N$ gives $t\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_I)$: since $h=N(t)\circ\eta_I$, its transpose is $\varepsilon^{A}_J\circ A_UN(t)\circ A_U(\eta_I)=t\circ\varepsilon^{A}_{A_UI}\circ A_U(\eta_I)=t$ by counit naturality and the triangle identity. Thus $v\circ a_C=t\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_I)$. Localizing this equality and identifying $QJ$ with $A_UF$ via $Q(t)$ shows that the derived transpose of $Q(d)$ is $A_U(\varepsilon^e_F)\circ a_{u,r_uF}^{-1}$. This is precisely $q_{u,F}$ in the canonical-mate statement. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $Q(d)=b_{u,F}$ with its specified normalization.

proof.text: Choose a degree-q global cocycle z in Gamma(U_et,I) representing x. The etale edge section is its class [z] in H^q(C), by the resolution description in the statement. The module-sheaf cohomology definition is kernel modulo image; hence a chain map sends the class of a cocycle to the class of its image, and sends boundaries to boundaries. Exactness of A_V identifies A_V H^q(C) with H^q(A_V C), naturally for d. Step 2 therefore gives H^q(d)(A_V([z]))=[h(z)] as global sections on V_proet. Step 1 identifies the global class of h(z) with c^q_{U,F}(x), so its class in H^q(D) is the pro-etale edge section of that class. Substitute Q(d)=b_{u,F} from Step 3 to obtain exactly the asserted equality. The same calculation covers q=0, the zero sheaf, the identity morphism, and empty U.

title: Etale/pro-etale comparison preserves higher-image edge sections
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and let $u:U\to V$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Use the small etale and pro-etale sites and their constant-ring module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For each scheme $T$, write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, placed in degree zero, and let $q\geq0$.
Use the canonical counit-mate direct-image comparison
$$b_{u,F}:A_VRu_{\mathrm{et},*}F\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_UF$$
of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Let
$$c^q_{U,F}:H^q(U_{\mathrm{et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A_UF)$$
be the comparison induced by the derived comparison unit as in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Under the canonical Leray identifications, let $e^q_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $e^q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the edge maps from these global cohomology groups to $\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{et}},R^qu_{\mathrm{et},*}F)$ and $\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{proet}},R^qu_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_UF)$, respectively: on an injective-resolution representative they send a global cocycle to its class in the cohomology sheaf of the direct-image complex [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For an etale section $s$ of $R^qu_{\mathrm{et},*}F$, let $A_V(s)$ denote its comparison pullback, using $A_V\Lambda_V\cong\Lambda_V$.
Then for every $x\in H^q(U_{\mathrm{et}},F)$,
$$
e^q_{\mathrm{proet}}(c^q_{U,F}(x))=
\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal H^q(b_{u,F}))\bigl(A_V(e^q_{\mathrm{et}}(x))\bigr),
$$
where $\mathcal H^q(A_VRu_{\mathrm{et},*}F)=A_VR^qu_{\mathrm{et},*}F$ is the exact-comparison identification.
